records.name: Tumour mutational burden (TMB)
records.tldr: Tumour mutational burden is an assay-defined density of eligible DNA mutations, usually reported per million bases.
records.summary: Tumour mutational burden divides eligible somatic mutation counts by an eligible DNA territory, commonly in mutations per megabase. Counting, origin filtering, calibration, specimen and quality rules affect the estimate. It does not directly measure immune recognition, copy-number instability or treatment response. A clinical threshold applies only within its validated assay and disease setting.

notes: TMB is the density of eligible somatic mutations over the assay reporting region, in mut/Mb (Mb = one million bases); the numerator rules, filters and any calibration are method-specific.
Panel, exome and genome examine different regions; a cancer-gene-enriched region need not behave as a random genomic sample.

When laboratories analysed the same exome data with their own regions and pipelines panel TMB estimates varied; this was a computational comparison, not proof of interchangeability for treatment selection.
More mutations offer more candidate neoantigens, but processing, HLA display and immune function still matter; high TMB neither guarantees checkpoint benefit nor establishes benefit in every cancer.

On 16 October 2026, FDA converted the U.S. tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab indication to traditional approval and changed its TMB-H criterion from 10 to at least 13 mutations per megabase. Section 1.18 covers adults and children with unresectable or metastatic solid tumours, measured by an FDA-authorised test, that have progressed after prior treatment and have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. This criterion does not replace thresholds in other indications or historical studies.

Fictional teaching exercise: 24 eligible mutations over 2 Mb is 12 mut/Mb and over 1 Mb is 24 mut/Mb; not comparable clinically without counting and calibration rules; a research result does not establish authorised-test eligibility.
TMB differs from copy-number instability and from MSI, and a TMB category does not settle an individual outcome.

Retain specimen type, DNA consumption, eligible mutation classes and reporting territory, germline/artefact filtering, calibration, mut/Mb, quality and uncertainty. Blood and tissue estimates need separate validation. Low tumour signal and uneven coverage can bias the count; both analytical performance and clinical applicability must match the assay, cancer and setting.

The July 2026 pembrolizumab label describes the TMB supporting KEYNOTE-158 analysis as a prospectively planned retrospective analysis of ten nonrandomized cohorts. That design does not establish TMB-based selection for early triple-negative breast cancer; retain the population, endpoint and clinical setting with the evidence.

Lung cancer is where tumour mutational burden was discovered as a predictor of checkpoint benefit (Rizvi 2015) and where it failed as a selector. The biology holds: burden tracks outcome within every PD-L1 stratum in 1,552 patients and is independent of PD-L1 (Rizvi 2018, Ricciuti 2022). The measurement does not: three units are in use (per megabase on a panel, per exome on sequencing, a plasma score), the best data-derived threshold was more than 19 per megabase rather than the licensed 10, and the association vanishes entirely once chemotherapy is added to the checkpoint inhibitor (Garassino 2023). It selects for single-agent immunotherapy only (Mok 2023).

records.name: Microsatellite instability (MSI-H) / mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR)
records.tldr: Microsatellite instability describes altered DNA repeats; mismatch-repair deficiency concerns the machinery that corrects copying errors.
records.summary: Mismatch repair normally corrects certain DNA copying errors. Defects can produce unstable short repeats, measured by defined DNA tests. Repair-protein staining examines another layer and requires appropriate controls. MSI-high, stable and indeterminate results retain their own assay definitions. Neither a tumour finding nor a retained stain alone diagnoses inherited risk, proves all repair function or guarantees treatment response.

links.label: Wikipedia
FDA pembrolizumab label revised July 2026
CAP 2022 MMR/MSI recommendations

notes: Microsatellites are short repeats; MSI is altered repeats in tumour DNA; MMR corrects some copying errors; dMMR lets repeat changes accumulate.
PCR or validated sequencing observes repeat instability; IHC observes staining for MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6; they ask different questions and neither is a complete repair test.
MSI-H, MSS and indeterminate are assay labels; an inadequate or indeterminate specimen must keep that label rather than become MSS.
CAP recommends cancer-type-specific validation for cancers outside better-established settings and says TMB should not be used as a surrogate for MMR status.
A tumour MSI or dMMR finding does not alone diagnose Lynch syndrome; some colorectal tumours lose MLH1 by methylation.

The U.S. pembrolizumab label section 1.8 covers unresectable or metastatic MSI-H or dMMR solid tumours, as determined by an FDA-authorised test, that progressed after prior treatment with no satisfactory alternatives; this is a reason to measure accurately, not a guarantee of response.
Fictional teaching exercise: Retained IHC staining with an indeterminate DNA MSI result cannot be reported as confirmed MSS; keep both results.

DNA repeat analysis and repair-protein staining use different material and controls: extraction consumes DNA; staining consumes tissue sections. Keep the named repeat algorithm or each protein stain, adequate tumour content, controls, quality and any discordance. No universal instability fraction or staining shortcut fits all cancers; inadequate material, failed controls and degraded samples need explicit labels and review.

Colorectal cancer: 10 to 15% of resected disease but only about 5% of first-line metastatic disease (153 of 3,063; Venderbosch 2014) and 3.5% in one advanced cohort (Koopman 2009), because unstable tumours metastasise less readily. The mechanism that makes them cancers is slippage in coding microsatellites: TGFBR2 was the first such target identified (Markowitz 1995), and ACVR2A, RNF43 and B2M follow. The mechanism that makes them treatable is mutation load, a mean of 1,782 somatic mutations against 73 in proficient tumours (Le 2015).

records.name: Next-generation sequencing (NGS)
records.tldr: Next-generation sequencing reads many prepared DNA or RNA-derived fragments in parallel, with detection limited by the chosen workflow.
records.summary: Sequencing infers base order from prepared material. Panels target selected regions; exomes primarily target exons; genomes cover coding and noncoding territory broadly. None guarantees uniform usable local evidence or analysis of every alteration class. Read length, territory, molecule independence, quality and validated use are separate features. Methylation requires an appropriate preparation and analysis rather than a sequencing category name.

Characterizing reduced coverage regions through comparison of exome and genome sequencing data across 10 centers.
Guidelines for Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Oncology Panels: A Joint Consensus Recommendation of the Association for Molecular Pathology and College of American Pathologists.

notes: Keep read counts distinct from independent molecules: paired ends and amplified copies can share a fragment. Base quality and mapping quality address different uncertainties. Usable local depth depends on explicit filters, including treatment of duplicate and overlapping reads. Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-depth.html, samtools 1.25 manual.

Fictional coverage exercise: if 900 of 1,000 target bases reach a stated 20-read criterion, breadth at that criterion is 90%. A mean of 100 reads per position does not establish adequate measurement at a particular position with four usable reads. These are teaching values, not diagnostic thresholds.
Targeted panel, exome and genome differ in intended territory; check exact coordinates and analysed change classes rather than gene count.
Exons include untranslated sequence; exome does not mean every captured base codes for protein nor that regulatory regions or rearrangement breakpoints were examined.
Ng et al. (2009) introductory scale estimates: Human genome is about 3,000 Mb; protein-coding sequence is about 1%, roughly 30 Mb across about 180,000 exons.

Zehir et al. (2017), prospective advanced-cancer cohort and computational downsampling: One hospital panel (MSK-IMPACT) covered 341 genes (2,809 tumours) then 410 (8,136 tumours) at mean 718x; downsampling to 150x exome depth would have missed at least 9% of mutations.

At a fixed budget broader territory commonly spreads reads thinner, but actual depth depends on design and usable yield; broader territory guarantees neither uniform sensitivity nor all-variant detection.
Territory labels do not specify performance for small variants, copy number or rearrangements, and conventional WGS does not automatically measure methylation.
Reduced-coverage regions exist even in clinical exome and genome workflows, including clinically relevant genes.
Fictional teaching exercise: A research genome negative at a repeat does not supersede a validated panel; a panel that never examines a fusion breakpoint cannot exclude it by a negative report.

Compare assays by accepted specimen, input consumption, designed coordinates, analysed alteration classes, local usable depth and breadth, quality filters and validated detection limits. Degradation, capture gaps and ambiguous repeats can defeat broad designs. Extraction uses material; the name panel, exome or genome supplies neither a tissue requirement nor clinical validation.

Lung cancer: NICE NG122 (1.2.12) says to see the National Genomics Test Directory for guidance on next-generation sequencing panels to guide treatment. In practice this is the single test that decides between tablets, immunotherapy and chemotherapy for most people with advanced non-squamous disease, which is why waiting a short time for the result is usually a better decision than starting quickly on the wrong route. The NHS explains that your hospital specialist requests the test, usually on a sample already taken.

records.name: RNA sequencing & expression profiling
records.tldr: RNA sequencing measures captured RNA messages and, with a suitable library and analysis, can examine transcript joins.
records.summary: RNA normally carries and helps process cellular messages. Sequencing captures part of that RNA information through a defined preparation and analysis. Pooled abundance, transcript structure and cell origin are separate questions. A supported RNA join does not automatically establish a DNA rearrangement, functional protein or treatment benefit.

links.label: Wikipedia
Deep RNA sequencing analysis of readthrough gene fusions in human prostate adenocarcinoma and reference samples.
Anchored multiplex PCR for targeted next-generation sequencing.
A new view of transcriptome complexity and regulation through the lens of local splicing variations.
Accuracy assessment of fusion transcript detection via read-mapping and de novo fusion transcript assembly-based methods.
10x fixed RNA probe chemistry, Cell Ranger 7.2

notes: RNA abundance and RNA structure are distinct measurements. Gene-level totals can conceal splice products. Some workflows sequence synthetic probes rather than original transcript-derived material; their counts cannot establish arbitrary fusion or splice sequences. Sources: Conesa et al., methods review, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8; official fixed RNA profiling chemistry, https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/7.2/getting-started/cr-flex-what-is-frp.

An RNA join does not by itself establish a DNA rearrangement. Readthrough messages were observed in prostate tumour and reference samples. Authenticate independent sequence support and evaluate the genomic mechanism, protein consequence and clinical significance separately. Source: Nacu et al., 2011, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21261984/.

Splice junctions join transcript regions and many are normal; a fusion transcript has sequence from different genes; an RNA junction does not establish the DNA mechanism; neighbouring-gene readthrough occurs in tumour and reference tissue.

A split read maps across the junction; a spanning pair places two ends on opposite sides leaving the insert unsequenced; amplified copies are not independent molecules; benchmark thresholds are not clinical cutoffs.

PSI is an inclusion estimate for a defined event and denominator; local junction evidence does not reconstruct a full transcript; unfinished nuclear RNA with introns is not automatically pathological intron retention.

Whole-transcriptome, short-end counting and targeted panels recover different information; anchored multiplex PCR searches from a targeted gene end toward an unknown partner and was tested in FFPE in the original method, which does not validate later panels.
Fixed-RNA probe-ligation counts are not unrestricted fusion or splice sequence evidence.
Failure to detect a join is informative only within coverage and sensitivity; RNA support leaves DNA mechanism, protein effect and drug benefit as separate tests.
Fictional teaching exercise: A candidate A-B junction supported by three identical amplified reads cannot be called confirmed DNA rearrangement or effective target.

Use protocol-compatible RNA and record aliquot consumption, integrity, reference/transcript versions, partners, junction coordinates and independent read/molecule support. State the event denominator for splice fractions. Low expression, uncovered joins, degradation, similar sequence and preparation/assembly artefacts constrain detection. Validate support thresholds, event classes and confirmation for the exact panel and specimen; a caller name supplies no clinical validation.

Pancreatic cancer: RNA sequencing does two jobs here, calling the classical versus basal-like subtype that predicts chemotherapy response (O'Kane 2020, Rashid 2020) and catching the NRG1, ALK, NTRK, FGFR2 and RET fusions that DNA panels miss in KRAS wild-type tumours (Philip 2022).

Lung cancer: RNA is the only reliable route to the fusions with heterogeneous partners. NRG1 fusions were found in 41 of 21,858 tumours by anchored multiplex RNA sequencing with a different partner almost every time (Jonna 2019), and the founding CD74-NRG1 discovery came from transcriptome sequencing of driver-negative tumours (Fernandez-Cuesta 2014). In small-cell disease RNA is also how the four transcriptional subtypes are called (Gay 2021).

RNA adds fusions that DNA testing misses: in 67,278 patients with both, RNA plus DNA sequencing found 21 per cent more driver gene fusions than DNA alone (Gai 2025, Tempus authors). On the large approved DNA and RNA panels the FDA approval often covers only part of what is reported: the approval statement for Caris MI Cancer Seek names DNA content only, while the maker lists RNA expression and fusions as additional features.
records.principle: A common workflow reverse-transcribes RNA to complementary DNA for sequencing. Other chemistries, including probe-based counting, require their own interpretation of the captured signal.
strengths: Captured transcript abundance with defined comparison rules
Fusion and splice evidence when the library and analysis cover the join
limitations: Preparation and RNA integrity affect recovery
RNA evidence does not directly measure protein function

records.name: Single-cell & spatial profiling
records.tldr: Bulk, cell or nucleus profiling, and spatial RNA methods attach measurements to different units and retain different context.
records.summary: Bulk RNA pools a specimen; cell or nucleus profiling separates recovered profiles; spatial methods retain capture positions or decoded molecule coordinates. Spots can contain several cells, and segmentation or imputation adds inference. Split aliquots and adjacent sections are not the same cells. Recovery, measured genes, physical resolution, replication and intended use determine which question each method can address.

links.label: Wikipedia
RNA imaging. Spatially resolved, highly multiplexed RNA profiling in single cells.
Cell type-specific gene expression differences in complex tissues.
Visualization and analysis of gene expression in tissue sections by spatial transcriptomics.
Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression.
Single-nucleus and single-cell transcriptomes compared in matched cortical cell types.

notes: Bulk RNA reports pooled abundance, cell or nucleus profiling reports recovered profiles, and spatial measurement attaches observations to tissue positions. A capture position can contain multiple cells. Directly observed RNA, cell assignments and model-imputed expression are distinct outputs. The original positional capture study examined mouse brain and human breast cancer tissue. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27365449/.

Fictional comparison exercise: 60 immune-assigned profiles among 300 recovered nuclei is 20% of recovered profiles. It does not establish 20% tissue area or original cell abundance. Split aliquots and adjacent sections are not the same cells. Biological replication and recovery bias still constrain cross-method comparisons. Source for biological-replicate requirements: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34584091/.
The axis that differs is the measured unit and the context still attached: pooled specimen, recovered cell or nucleus profile, or capture position or decoded molecule coordinates.
Estimating cell sources from a bulk mixture needs assumptions and references and is not direct counting.

Single-cell uses barcodes; whole cells capture nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA while nuclei mainly nuclear RNA; dissociation and filtering affect recovery; profile-based identity is an assignment, not proof of malignancy.

A spatial capture spot or bin can contain several cells; imaging locates decoded molecules but segmentation affects cell-level reading; observed molecule, assigned cell and imputed value are different outputs.
Adjacent sections or split aliquots are not the same cells; two libraries from one portion are technical repeats of one biological specimen.
Cells from one specimen are not independent biological replicates.
Fictional teaching exercise: Of 300 recovered nuclei, 60 immune is 20% of recovered nuclei, not a tissue-area or original-cell fraction.

Budget finite tissue, aliquots and sections for each compatible preparation. Report counts or normalised abundance per pool, recovered cell/nucleus or spatial unit, with physical resolution, measured genes and cell-boundary rules. Quality criteria, recovery, processing/imaging/analysis cost and controls vary by assay. Independent specimens support biological comparisons; attractive maps and technical repeats do not provide clinical validation.

OnCo reading inference: finer spatial resolution does not automatically provide broader measured-gene coverage or more complete recovery. A missing RNA count can reflect preparation or detection limits; an inferred cell source or protein activity is a different kind of output.
records.principle: RNA is captured with barcodes per cell or per spatial location, or read by imaging-based in situ hybridisation for hundreds to thousands of genes.
strengths: Retains spatial context in compatible workflows
limitations: Preparation, recovery and analysis affect results
Clinical utility requires evidence for the intended use

records.name: Long-read sequencing (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore)
records.tldr: Long reads connect extended sequence information; chemical-mark detection requires a separately specified workflow.
records.summary: Long-read sequencing can connect variants, repeats and rearrangement boundaries on extended molecules. DNA methylation is a chemical feature requiring native-signal inference or an appropriate conversion workflow. Long sequence alone does not establish that modification analysis occurred. Preparation, molecule integrity, supported caller and controls constrain the result; neither sequence nor a methylation fraction alone establishes gene function or treatment benefit.

links.label: Logsdon et al., Long-read human genome sequencing and its applications (Nature Reviews Genetics 2020)
A genomic sequencing protocol that yields a positive display of 5-methylcytosine residues in individual DNA strands.
Detecting DNA cytosine methylation using nanopore sequencing.
Genome-wide detection of cytosine methylation by single molecule real-time sequencing.

notes: Long sequence connections and chemical-mark detection require separately specified workflows. Nanopore methylation inference uses native current signals and a trained modification model; ordinary sequence letters alone do not supply that analysis. Source: Simpson et al., 2017 method experiment, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28218898/.

Bisulfite conversion encodes methylation information before amplification; ordinary amplification of unconverted DNA does not faithfully preserve original methylation marks. The original bisulfite method tested defined genomic sequences, rather than clinical treatment selection. Source: Frommer et al., 1992, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1542678/.

Fictional methylation exercise: eight called methylated molecules among ten usable molecules at one site gives 80%. That fraction does not establish 80% cancer cells or 80% gene silencing. Retain site, usable-molecule denominator, calling uncertainty and specimen mixture.
Long reads can span repeats, rearrangement boundaries and nearby variants, supporting phasing; the human reference-genome experiment did not establish universal clinical detection in every tumour.
DNA methylation is a chemical modification, not a change in base sequence; detection needs a specific workflow.

Native nanopore current with a trained modification caller (Simpson 2017), SMRT polymerase kinetics with a validated model (Tse 2021) and bisulfite conversion (Frommer 1992) detect marks differently; a long-read report does not imply a modification analysis.
Ordinary amplification of unconverted DNA copies sequence without faithfully copying native marks; conversion encodes chemical state before amplification.
Long read and methylation assay are independent capabilities; a long RNA or cDNA read does not measure tumour DNA methylation.

Eight of ten usable molecules called methylated at one site is 80% of those molecules; it is not 80% malignant cells or 80% gene silencing; per-molecule confidence differs from a fraction across molecules.

Record the molecule type and integrity, aliquot used, library preparation, sequence and modification callers, and any retained native signals. Report sequence length separately from modification confidence or site fraction. Fragmentation, unsupported models, amplification and conversion failure have different effects. Input requirements, usable-site filters and intended-use validation belong to the exact assay.
records.principle: Connect extended molecule sequences; infer specified DNA marks only from a supported native-signal model or conversion-based workflow.
strengths: Extended sequence connections and phasing evidence
Modification information when supported by the exact workflow
limitations: Input integrity and usable site coverage

records.name: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and the full transcriptome
records.tldr: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a tissue sample, including contributions from multiple cell types.
records.summary: RNA carries cellular messages; bulk sequencing samples those messages from combined tissue after protocol-specific capture and preparation. Analysis assigns usable observations to genes or transcripts and applies a defined comparison scale. A change can reflect cell composition, expression within cells or both. Gene totals can conceal transcript differences, and pooled RNA does not directly establish protein localisation, pathway flux or drug dependence.

links.label: Wikipedia: transcriptome
Wikipedia
A comprehensive assessment of RNA-seq accuracy, reproducibility and information content by the Sequencing Quality Control Consortium.
A survey of best practices for RNA-seq data analysis.

notes: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a specimen. Cancer, immune and supporting cells can contribute different amounts of RNA; a higher signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells, or both. Zero detected reads does not establish biological absence. Source: Conesa et al., 2016 methods review, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8.

Name the counting unit and normalisation denominator. Estimated transcript counts, length-adjusted transcripts per million and tagged molecule counts answer different measurement questions. A gene total can conceal splice products; pooled RNA does not directly measure surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence. Sources: https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/file_formats.html and https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8.

Fictional mixture exercise: in two 100-cell samples, increasing identical marker-producing lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles their stipulated marker molecules if each contributes one and other cells contribute none. This does not show cancer-cell activation. Equal RNA contribution and matched recovery are assumptions, not measured tissue properties.
Bulk RNA-seq extracts RNA, prepares a library (often cDNA), may select mRNA or deplete rRNA or capture regions; bulk does not mean equal capture of all molecules.
Reads or fragments are assigned to genes or transcripts; shared sequences make assignment ambiguous; a count table is already shaped by preparation and analysis.
A bulk signal can rise because more cells of a type contribute, expression within them rises, or both; deconvolution estimates contributions under a model and does not separate cells.
Gene-level counts can hide isoform differences; a mutant or splice product needs sequence or junction evidence.

Bulk RNA can nominate expressed targets and summarise programmes but does not establish cell origin, surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence; zero reads is not absence; thousands of genes from one biopsy are not thousands of patients.

Fictional teaching exercise: With equal RNA per cell, a lymphocyte-only marker and 100-cell pieces, raising lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles the pooled marker (20 to 40 stipulated molecules) without changing any cancer cell.
Record sampled region and RNA integrity; research profiling differs from a validated clinical RNA test.

Record protocol-compatible preservation, sampled region, RNA integrity and material consumed by extraction. Track capture, sequence assignment, read/fragment units, normalisation and transcript calls. Preparation time varies; reference material, process controls and biological replicates test different uncertainties. Degradation, contamination, ambiguous annotation, batch and mixture shifts constrain purpose-specific cutoffs and clinical intended-use validation.

records.name: Variant calling
records.tldr: Variant calling evaluates sequence evidence and error models to identify candidate changes within a defined assay scope.
records.summary: Variant calling assesses whether observed sequence or regional evidence supports a difference from a reference or comparison sample. Evidence quality, independent fragments, local depth, error models and the alteration class matter. Annotation describes possible consequence after calling; neither annotation nor a passed filter independently proves function or treatment relevance. Negative calls retain the workflow coverage and detection limits.

links.label: Lawrence et al., Mutational heterogeneity in cancer and the search for new cancer-associated genes (MutSigCV, Nature 2013)
Wikipedia
Sensitive detection of somatic point mutations in impure and heterogeneous cancer samples.
Guidelines for Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Oncology Panels: A Joint Consensus Recommendation of the Association for Molecular Pathology and College of American Pathologists.

notes: Base quality concerns confidence in a sequence letter; mapping quality concerns its proposed location. A clear letter can still map ambiguously. Depth depends on the chosen quality, duplicate and overlapping-pair filters, so retain these rules with support counts. Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-depth.html, samtools 1.25 manual.

Passing a computational filter does not establish biological function or treatment benefit. Agreement between callers using the same reads does not create independent molecular evidence; a shared mapping problem can remain. The exact regions, alteration classes and usable local evidence constrain a negative result.

Variant calling evaluates sequence evidence and error models to identify candidate differences; methods are class-specific (substitutions, indels, copy changes, rearrangements) and a workflow calling one class may not call another.
Evidence includes usable depth, base and mapping quality, strand and fragment distribution and comparison-sample support; somatic callers must handle low-frequency evidence in mixed samples.
In VCF, PASS means the call passed the stated filters; a dot means filters have not been applied; counts and allele fractions need defined denominators.
Annotation adds gene or predicted consequence and is separate from calling; machine learning is one method, not the definition.
Two callers agreeing on shared reads can share misalignment error; confirmation needs an independent suitable method; a negative call set is bounded by detectable regions, classes and fractions.
Fictional teaching exercise: A call that is PASS in two tools but supported only by reads aligning ambiguously to duplicated regions has not resolved location.

Calling uses existing reads, a reference assembly and optional comparison files; a new confirmation assay can consume more material. Report coordinates, alleles, support, quality, filters and defined fractions/copy estimates. Retain caller version, detectable regions/classes and thresholds. Contamination, damage, misalignment and reference mismatch require specimen-specific end-to-end validation; filter thresholds are not treatment thresholds.

records.name: Batch effects and harmonisation
records.tldr: A batch effect is a systematic measurement difference associated with how samples were prepared, processed or analysed.
records.summary: Technical conditions can shift molecular measurements and become confused with biological groups. Normalization and batch modelling address specified effects under assumptions; they cannot manufacture contrasts absent from the design. Biological changes in tissue mixture should not automatically be removed as technical variation. Controls, recorded metadata, distributed preparation and independent replication help evaluate the comparison.

sva Bioconductor package (ComBat)
Wikipedia
Normalization of RNA-seq data using factor analysis of control genes or samples.
Reproducibility of high-throughput mRNA and small RNA sequencing across laboratories.

notes: Record preparation, laboratory, protocol and analysis conditions before comparing RNA profiles. The GEUVADIS study examined lymphoblastoid cell lines across laboratories; its reproducibility findings apply to that design and do not validate every tumour preparation. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.2702.

Fictional design exercise: if all baseline specimens use laboratory A and all follow-up specimens use laboratory B, the observed difference cannot separate laboratory from time. Correction cannot supply the missing crossed comparison. A changed tissue mixture can be real biology; a tidy corrected plot alone does not establish a treatment effect.
A batch effect is a systematic measurement difference tied to preparation, processing or analysis conditions that can be mistaken for biology; a batch is a group sharing a technical condition.

Normalisation adjusts defined aspects such as library size or composition and does not automatically remove gene-specific technical differences; models can include recorded batch variables; controls and repeat preparations help under assumptions.
When every sample of one group is processed one way and every sample of another group another way the effects cannot be separately identified; an algorithm cannot supply the missing experiment.
Cell mixture and treatment response can be real biology; erasing them as batch removes signal; a tidy corrected plot is not proof.
Reprocessing one extract is a technical, not a biological, replicate.
Multi-laboratory RNA-seq work shows why preparation conditions should be recorded.

Assess technical variation using preparation metadata, appropriate controls, diagnostic plots and a defined design/model. Reanalysis uses no new tissue; new preparations use extract and resequencing can use an existing library. Acceptance criteria depend on the comparison. Missing metadata, complete confounding and removal of genuine biology can invalidate correction; check assumptions and reproducibility rather than a universal batch-size cutoff.

Fictional design exercise: six baseline specimens in lab A and six follow-up specimens in lab B leave two group-laboratory cells unobserved. Allocating three to each of the four cells retains six per time point while adding the crossed contrasts. The design supports a stated model, with other biases and assumptions still requiring checks.

records.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq, 10x Chromium)
records.tldr: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing profile captured messages assigned to recovered cells or nuclei.
records.summary: RNA is distributed across cellular compartments. Whole-cell and nucleus preparations sample different material and can recover different populations. Barcodes label captured profiles rather than certifying one intact cell; quality, ambient RNA and doublet checks remain necessary. Sparse capture and selective recovery prevent a complete census, and many profiles from one biopsy do not create independent patient replicates.

notes: A barcode identifies a captured reaction profile, requiring checks for ambient RNA and multiple contributing cells. Whole-cell and isolated-nucleus preparations sample different compartments; recovered profiles are not a complete tissue census. A zero count does not establish biological absence. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28091601/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33367645/.

Differential-expression comparisons must account for variation between biological replicates. Source: Squair et al., 2021, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34584091/.

Check library chemistry before seeking sequence variants or splice junctions. In the documented fixed RNA profiling workflow, synthetic ligated probes are sequenced rather than captured-transcript complementary DNA. Gene counts from that workflow do not provide unrestricted original transcript sequence. Source: https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/7.2/getting-started/cr-flex-what-is-frp.
A barcode labels a reaction compartment and a UMI separates captured molecules from amplified copies, giving a gene-by-barcode table; a barcode does not guarantee one intact cell.

Single-nucleus sequencing samples nuclear RNA including unfinished transcripts with introns, whole cells also capture cytoplasmic messages; a mouse cortex study showed different recovery; not proof nuclei are better for tumours.
Dissociation can lose fragile cells; nuclei can come from frozen tissue; fixed-material probe methods count ligated probes and cannot reveal every variant or splice product.
A zero can be a missed molecule (dropout) rather than absence; ambient RNA contaminates profiles; a doublet combines cells or nuclei; correction does not certify every barcode.
A cluster groups similar profiles and does not prove malignancy, lineage or a clone; cancer-cell identification needs supporting evidence.
Thousands of cells from one biopsy are nested in one biological sample; splitting into two libraries does not create two patients; replicate-level aggregation is one approach.

Record compatible viable/frozen/fixed preparation, material used, chemistry, cell/nucleus recovery and quality/identity checks. Report a gene-by-barcode table with its UMI/read/probe counting unit. Cell calling, low-quality and doublet criteria are chemistry/version-specific. Selective recovery, sparse capture, ambient RNA, degradation and batch require validation; a platform name provides neither a complete census nor clinical validity.

records.name: Tumour mutational burden testing
records.tldr: Tumour mutational burden testing estimates eligible mutation density using a specified assay and reporting territory.
records.summary: A TMB test reports eligible somatic mutation density after assay-specific counting, filtering and calibration. The reporting territory, specimen, local measurement quality and inherited-variant handling affect the number. Computational harmonisation comparisons show why identical units do not make assays interchangeable. A research estimate alone does not establish the test and disease-setting requirements of a clinical indication.

links.label: FDA: pembrolizumab approval for TMB-H solid tumours (2020)
FDA pembrolizumab label revised July 2026
Merino et al. (2020), in-silico TMB harmonization
FDA, 16 October 2026: traditional approval and updated TMB-H indication
KEYTRUDA current prescribing information, sections 1.18 and 2.1

notes: TMB is the density of eligible somatic mutations over the assay reporting region, in mut/Mb (Mb = one million bases); the numerator rules, filters and any calibration are method-specific.
Panel, exome and genome examine different regions; a cancer-gene-enriched region need not behave as a random genomic sample.

When laboratories analysed the same exome data with their own regions and pipelines panel TMB estimates varied; this was a computational comparison, not proof of interchangeability for treatment selection.
More mutations offer more candidate neoantigens, but processing, HLA display and immune function still matter; high TMB neither guarantees checkpoint benefit nor establishes benefit in every cancer.

On 16 October 2026, FDA converted the U.S. tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab indication to traditional approval and changed its TMB-H criterion from 10 to at least 13 mutations per megabase. Section 1.18 covers adults and children with unresectable or metastatic solid tumours, measured by an FDA-authorised test, that have progressed after prior treatment and have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. This criterion does not replace thresholds in other indications or historical studies.

Fictional teaching exercise: 24 eligible mutations over 2 Mb is 12 mut/Mb and over 1 Mb is 24 mut/Mb; not comparable clinically without counting and calibration rules; a research result does not establish authorised-test eligibility.
TMB differs from copy-number instability and from MSI, and a TMB category does not settle an individual outcome.

Retain specimen type, DNA consumption, eligible mutation classes and reporting territory, germline/artefact filtering, calibration, mut/Mb, quality and uncertainty. Blood and tissue estimates need separate validation. Low tumour signal and uneven coverage can bias the count; both analytical performance and clinical applicability must match the assay, cancer and setting.

The July 2026 pembrolizumab label describes the TMB supporting KEYNOTE-158 analysis as a prospectively planned retrospective analysis of ten nonrandomized cohorts. That design does not establish TMB-based selection for early triple-negative breast cancer; retain the population, endpoint and clinical setting with the evidence.

Lung cancer: the measurement is sound and the threshold is not. Panel estimates track whole-exome estimates at rho 0.86 (Rizvi 2018) and blood-based estimates work without tissue (Gandara 2018), but the three units, mutations per megabase on a panel, mutations per exome on sequencing and a plasma score, are not interchangeable, the data-derived cut in the largest cohort was more than 19 rather than 10 per megabase (Ricciuti 2022), and the whole signal disappears in the chemo-immunotherapy setting where most patients are treated (Garassino 2023).
records.principle: Count eligible somatic variants under specified filtering and calibration rules, then normalise to eligible megabases.
limitations: Assay, territory and specimen affect estimates
A biomarker category does not guarantee benefit

records.name: HLA loss of heterozygosity
records.tldr: Loss of an inherited HLA gene version can change which peptide-presenting molecules a tumour retains.
records.summary: Human leukocyte antigen molecules normally present peptides to immune cells. HLA loss of heterozygosity concerns which inherited DNA versions remain in the sampled tumour, separately from their expression or current peptide display.

links.label: Allele-Specific HLA Loss and Immune Escape in Lung Cancer Evolution.
HGNC: HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C gene locations

notes: HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C are on chromosome 6. HGNC places HLA-A at 6p22.1 and HLA-B and HLA-C at 6p21.33. One inherited version of each locus comes from each parent, giving up to six distinct classical class-I alleles. A segmental loss can affect several linked loci; total copy count alone does not identify which inherited versions remain.

McGranahan et al. (2017): LOHHLA found HLA LOH in 36 of 90 (40%) TRACERx non-small-cell lung cancers; it used patient-specific HLA sequences with purity and ploidy; not a prevalence for every breast cancer.
A loss may be present in one tumour population; normal and other tumour cells contribute reads; weak or indeterminate calls are not proof of retention; one region does not map every lesion.
DNA loss, reduced allele-specific RNA, reduced surface protein and B2M functional loss are separate findings; B2M loss affects many alleles at once.
A credible loss call asks which proposed targets depend on the lost allele and what supports presentation through retained alleles; it does not show all targets fail.
Fictional teaching exercise: Loss of a maternal haplotype carrying A*X, B*Y, C*Z challenges peptides predicted for A*X and for B*Y; retention of paternal alleles does not itself prove display.

Retain tumour/normal material, typing, named HLA alleles, usable reads, inferred allele copies, confidence, caller version and region sampled. DNA extraction uses material; computational reanalysis does not. Incorrect typing, difficult mapping and low tumour content can obscure loss. Coverage and statistical rules require workflow validation; neither a negative call nor retained DNA proves current display.

The LOHHLA PCR validation selected 82 regions from 27 tumours predicted to have either all three loci affected by LOH or none. This selection does not establish how often a typical tumour region loses all three loci. The 36-of-90 result describes the separate NSCLC cohort analysis.

records.name: Sequencing depth and coverage
records.tldr: Depth counts sequence observations at a position; breadth describes how much of a target meets a stated depth.
records.summary: Depth is the number of aligned reads covering a base after stated filters; 40x means forty counted observations under those rules; depth without its counting rule is incomplete.

links.label: Guidelines for Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Oncology Panels: A Joint Consensus Recommendation of the Association for Molecular Pathology and College of American Pathologists.
samtools depth counting rules
samtools coverage summary rules

notes: Depth is the number of aligned reads covering a base after stated filters; 40x means forty counted observations under those rules; depth without its counting rule is incomplete.

Mean depth averages positions; coverage breadth is the fraction of a named target (denominator: target bases, not reads or cells) meeting a stated minimum depth; neither shows which important positions were missed.

Fictional report: mean 100x, 900 of 1,000 target bases at or above an illustrative 20x criterion gives 90% breadth, while the position of interest has 4 usable observations; 20x is not a clinical cutoff.

Read depth differs from molecular depth: overlapping pair ends and amplification copies inflate reads without adding independent fragments; HTSlib defaults are software definitions, not clinical validation criteria.
More sequencing cannot recover a region absent from the library or create independent molecules from duplicates; library complexity, input, preservation, capture and alignment limit usable evidence.

A negative report covers tested regions, detectable change classes and validated sensitivity; identical depths can support different detection limits; depth does not establish origin, function or actionability.
A narrow panel can be deep and a genome broad but thinner per position; territory asks where, depth asks how many.

Use an existing alignment file to calculate depth without consuming more tissue; recovering a more diverse library may require another aliquot. Retain reference regions, per-position counts, summary depth, breadth criterion and molecule-count rules. Capture bias, duplicate inflation and damaged input require controls and intended-use sensitivity/reproducibility validation; a summary criterion is separate from a detection limit.

records.name: Sequencing reads
records.tldr: A sequencing read records base letters from prepared material, with estimates of their quality.
records.summary: A read is an instrument-derived base sequence from a prepared library molecule with per-base quality; library preparation can copy, shorten or select molecules before sequencing.

links.label: Guidelines for Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Oncology Panels: A Joint Consensus Recommendation of the Association for Molecular Pathology and College of American Pathologists.
Base-calling of automated sequencer traces using phred. II. Error probabilities.
SAM specification

notes: A read is an instrument-derived base sequence from a prepared library molecule with per-base quality; library preparation can copy, shorten or select molecules before sequencing.

Phred quality: Q20 is an estimated 1% per-base error probability and Q30 0.1%; these are model-based base-call estimates, not the probability that a reported mutation is real; Q30 is a scale value, not a universal pass rule.
Base quality (a letter) and mapping confidence (a location) are separate; repeats can make placement ambiguous; one read can have more than one proposed alignment record.
Paired-end reads come from opposite ends of one fragment, so they are complementary placement evidence, not two independent molecules.

Amplification copies one fragment many times; duplicate recognition or validated molecular tags assess independent support but do not repair errors introduced before tagging; in amplicon assays identical start and end coordinates cannot separate copies from independent molecules.
Raw versus usable reads: filtering changes the denominator for downstream support; a read does not identify a cell, establish function or alone prove a somatic mutation.

Record extraction and library preparation, specimen compatibility, read lengths, base qualities, pairs, alignment records and molecule-support rules. Preparation consumes material; reanalysis does not. Contamination, damaged molecules, adapters, amplification and mapping ambiguity affect support. Filter settings and Q30 are not universal clinical acceptance criteria; validate the complete specimen-to-report workflow.

records.name: Tumor-normal versus tumor-only sequencing
records.tldr: Comparing tumour and suitable normal DNA helps distinguish acquired changes from inherited ones.
records.summary: A matched normal is a separately collected specimen from the same person chosen to represent constitutional DNA; normal is an analytical role, not a guarantee of uncomplicated cells; it differs from a healthy reference cohort.

links.label: Personalized genomic analyses for cancer mutation discovery and interpretation.
Guidelines for Validation of Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Oncology Panels: A Joint Consensus Recommendation of the Association for Molecular Pathology and College of American Pathologists.

notes: A matched normal is a separately collected specimen from the same person chosen to represent constitutional DNA; normal is an analytical role, not a guarantee of uncomplicated cells; it differs from a healthy reference cohort.

Evidence in the normal supports constitutional origin; adequate tumour and normal depth with no normal support supports somatic origin; inadequate normal depth leaves an attribution gap and absence there is uninformative.

Tumour-only workflows infer origin from population databases, allele fractions and models; rare germline variants may be absent from databases; a hotspot or familiar gene does not prove tumour-only origin.

In Jones et al. (2015), 815 tumour-normal pairs across 15 tumour types, germline changes in cancer-predisposing genes were found in 3% of patients with apparently sporadic cancers; tumour-only analysis could not definitively identify them and added false positives of 31% (targeted) and 65% (exome) of alterations.
Origin does not establish function, hereditary-risk conclusions or drug benefit; paired research sequencing is not a validated hereditary test.

Fictional teaching exercise: A tumour-only rare repair-gene variant at 48% allele fraction absent from databases cannot be labelled inherited or somatic from those facts; review copy state and attribution model.

Retain specimen identity, suitable normal tissue, extraction consumption, reference coordinates, both support counts and fractions, attribution rules and uncertainty. Normal sampling need not require a second tumour biopsy. Mismatch, contamination, low normal coverage and rare constitutional variants can mislead; validate the intended somatic/germline workflow and confirmation policy separately.

records.name: Gene-expression signatures
records.tldr: An expression signature combines measured gene messages using a defined scoring method.
records.summary: A signature combines selected RNA measurements by a defined algorithm; preprocessing, weights, reference data and software version are part of the definition; a gene list alone is not a test.

links.label: Gene set enrichment analysis: a knowledge-based approach for interpreting genome-wide expression profiles.
Supervised risk predictor of breast cancer based on intrinsic subtypes.
Most random gene expression signatures are significantly associated with breast cancer outcome.
Criteria for the use of omics-based predictors in clinical trials: explanation and elaboration.
Seurat AddModuleScore definition

notes: A signature combines selected RNA measurements by a defined algorithm; preprocessing, weights, reference data and software version are part of the definition; a gene list alone is not a test.
Pattern or module score, subtype classifier and outcome predictor answer different questions; performance belongs to a population, endpoint and horizon.
The original PAM50 work used a defined 50-gene method for intrinsic subtypes and risk models and does not validate every later similar score.
Seurat's AddModuleScore subtracts matched control-gene expression from the selected-gene mean; GSEA tests accumulation toward one end of a ranked list; outputs cannot share a cutoff.

A clinical predictor needs a locked procedure; in the Venet et al. (2011) breast-cancer analysis, more than 90% of random signatures over 100 genes were significant outcome predictors, so association alone does not show the named biology matters.
Analytical repeatability, clinical validity and clinical utility are separate questions.
A bulk inflammatory signature can rise from more immune cells, changed state or both; a stress score does not establish protein activation, metabolic rate or dependence.
Fictional teaching exercise: Replacing normalisation while retaining the old high cutoff is not validated; the old cutoff cannot supply missing validation.

An expression score requires compatible RNA input, locked preprocessing, genes, weights, reference, endpoint/horizon and software version. Existing data can be rescored without new tissue; acquiring RNA consumes material. Report categories, ranks, probabilities or unitless scores on their exact scale. Missing genes, batch, mixture and population shift undermine cutoffs; analytical, clinical and utility evidence remain separate.

records.name: Immune deconvolution
records.tldr: Deconvolution estimates which cell populations contributed to a mixed molecular measurement.
records.summary: Deconvolution fits reference cell-type profiles to a mixed profile under a model; similar types, missing populations and state change allow several fits.

links.label: Robust enumeration of cell subsets from tissue expression profiles.
Simultaneous enumeration of cancer and immune cell types from bulk tumor gene expression data.
Profiling Tumor Infiltrating Immune Cells with CIBERSORT.
Determining cell type abundance and expression from bulk tissues with digital cytometry.

notes: Deconvolution fits reference cell-type profiles to a mixed profile under a model; similar types, missing populations and state change allow several fits.
The first quantity can be a share of RNA, not cells; EPIC uses RNA-content assumptions and an uncharacterised component.

Relative estimates may sum to one across represented immune populations leaving total immune content unknown; CIBERSORT absolute mode is an expression-based score, not cells per area; other methods report whole-sample fractions.
CIBERSORTx infers cell-type expression and states; these are computational reconstructions, not single-cell measurements, and do not prove suppressive function, clone or location.
Compare with flow, pathology or spatial data, each with its own bias; validate for tissue, preparation, populations and units.
Fictional teaching exercise: Sample A has 10 T cells among 20 immune cells and sample B 30 among 60 (100 cells each): both 50% of immune cells, but 10% and 30% of the whole sample.

Existing mixture data and reference profiles support computation without further tissue; comparator assays may consume material. Record fit algorithm, reference, denominator, omitted populations and output as relative fraction, whole-sample estimate, abundance score or inferred expression. Runtime and fit filters vary; known mixtures, held-out data and matched measurements test assumptions. Similar signatures, RNA content, state and platform shifts prevent a global fit from certifying every population or clinical use.

records.name: RNA pathway scoring
records.tldr: A pathway score summarises selected gene messages under a defined method and comparison scale.
records.summary: Inputs are expression data, a gene set and scoring rules; shared genes make pathway scores related; two numbers called pathway score are not necessarily comparable.

links.label: Gene set enrichment analysis: a knowledge-based approach for interpreting genome-wide expression profiles.
GSVA: gene set variation analysis for microarray and RNA-seq data.
GSVA software vignette

notes: Inputs are expression data, a gene set and scoring rules; shared genes make pathway scores related; two numbers called pathway score are not necessarily comparable.

ssGSEA compares rank distributions inside and outside a set within a sample, with optional scaling that can involve the supplied score collection; GSVA estimates each gene's distribution across supplied samples first, so changing the cohort changes the comparison; the GSVA package also implements ssGSEA.
A score is commonly unitless and is not automatically a significance test or probability; a percentile ranks against a defined group, so the 90th percentile is not 90% activity.
RNA scores do not directly measure protein, phosphorylation, flux or dependence; feedback can raise messages while output falls; a response classifier needs its own locked model.
Fictional teaching exercise: Ranks A to E, set {A,C,E}: mean rank (1+3+5)/3=3; a teaching calculation, neither ssGSEA nor GSVA, and not an activity measure.
The original GSEA framework evaluated ranked expression evidence in cohort comparisons; its output is not interchangeable with every per-sample score.

Scoring existing RNA requires no additional tissue; functional tests may. Record gene IDs/set version, measured universe, input scale, parameters, algorithm and reference cohort. Report unitless scores, normalised scores or percentiles explicitly. Runtime and filters vary; replication and sensitivity to mixtures/missing genes test robustness. Overlapping sets, platform/composition shifts and changed cohorts constrain comparisons; activation and clinical cutoffs need separate validation.

records.name: Variant allele frequency (VAF)
records.tldr: Variant allele frequency is the fraction of informative reads or molecules that support a variant under a test’s definition. It is not directly the fraction of cancer cells.
records.summary: Read-based VAF divides variant-supporting reads by informative reads at the locus. Some assays instead report a molecule-based measure, so keep the laboratory’s definition. Tumor purity, local allele-specific copy number, ploidy, subclonal mixture and assay behavior affect the value. VAF alone cannot assign zygosity, variant origin, the number of clones or a cancer-cell percentage. Changes over time in plasma also require attention to specimen and non-tumor DNA contributors.

links.label: Li et al., Standards and guidelines for the interpretation and reporting of sequence variants in cancer: AMP, ASCO and CAP joint consensus (Journal of Molecular Diagnostics 2017)
Absolute quantification of somatic DNA alterations in human cancer.
Allele-specific genomic data elucidate the role of somatic gain and copy-number neutral loss of heterozygosity in cancer.
High-intensity sequencing reveals the sources of plasma circulating cell-free DNA variants.

notes: VAF is the proportion of usable reads or assay-defined molecules supporting the alternate sequence; keep the denominator: 25 of 100 usable observations is 25%.

CCF is carrier cancer cells over all sampled cancer cells; its inputs have distinct denominators: cell purity p, DNA contribution, pathology cellularity (method-defined, for RCB the tumour-bed area), global ploidy P, local copy number C, mutant multiplicity m.
With equal recovery per genome copy and diploid normals, tumour DNA contribution is p*P/[p*P+2*(1-p)]; half the cells at ploidy four contribute two thirds of DNA.

For uniform local copies, expected VAF is p*f*m/[p*C+(1-p)*2]; assumptions: two normal copies, uniform cancer copies, fixed multiplicity, unbiased observations; subclonal copy change needs a richer model.
Same 50 cancer plus 50 normal cells, every cancer cell carrying one variant copy: expected VAF 50/200=25% with two local cancer copies and 50/150 about 33% with one; CCF stays 100% and purity 50%.

Purity 0.5, one mutant copy: four local copies with CCF 100% and two local copies with CCF 2/3 both predict VAF 1/6 (about 16.7%); copy evidence separates them; CCF above 100% signals incompatible assumptions.

High VAF alone cannot establish truncal ancestry or origin or function; a rise after treatment can reflect mixture or copy change as well as carrier expansion; uncertain inputs give alternative CCF fits, not counted cells.

Retain DNA and copy-state inputs, filtered support denominators, fractions, local copies, multiplicity, purity, model version and alternative fits. New extraction consumes material; reanalysis alone does not. Artifacts, few molecules, recovery bias and uncertain copy/mixture estimates limit conversion. Detection thresholds and model-fit criteria do not establish a universal clonal-target cutoff or treatment benefit.

records.name: Gene amplification and copy-number change
records.tldr: Cancer cells often have extra copies of a growth gene (amplification) or have lost copies of a protective one (deletion), rather than a spelling change within the gene. Extra copies of HER2 or MYCN are classic examples that change treatment.
records.summary: Amplification (detected by FISH, ISH or NGS copy-number calls) can increase gene dosage and expression: HER2 in breast and gastric cancer, MYCN in high-risk neuroblastoma, MET amplification as a resistance route to EGFR inhibitors, CCNE1 in ovarian and gastric cancer, MDM2 in liposarcoma, CDK4 in glioma. Deletions remove tumour suppressors: del(17p)/TP53 in CLL and myeloma (predicting chemo-resistance), CDKN2A/B in glioma (defining grade 4), MTAP (creating a PRMT5 vulnerability), 9p21 loss linked to immunotherapy resistance. Loss of heterozygosity and larger chromosome changes contribute to some method-defined genomic-scar scores. Their clinical interpretation depends on the exact test, cancer and treatment setting; a copy state alone does not establish current repair function or drug benefit.

links.label: Wikipedia
Absolute quantification of somatic DNA alterations in human cancer.
Gene expression analysis identifies global gene dosage sensitivity in cancer.

notes: Total copy count, allele identity, RNA abundance and protein activity are separate measurements. Purity, ploidy and the assay’s definition affect copy calls. Fehrmann and colleagues related copy number to expression after modelling shared transcriptional components in large datasets; that association does not promise a fixed protein increase, target dependence or treatment benefit in a particular tumour.
Total copy number counts copies of a region; allele-specific copy number estimates the contributions of the distinguishable sequence versions A and B.
1+1 is two copies with both versions; 1+0 is one copy with LOH (deletion); 2+0 is copy-neutral LOH (two copies, one version); 2+1 is three copies with both versions retained.
LOH is not synonymous with deletion: copy-neutral LOH can follow loss plus duplication or recombination; a gain does not necessarily erase either version.

Major and minor counts are the larger and smaller allelic contributions; minor of zero supports LOH under the model; they do not identify parental origin or assign a mutation to a copy; phasing needs suitable evidence.
Local copy count differs from ploidy; relative signal can fit different purity and ploidy pairs; fractional counts can reflect mixture or subclonal states.

Methods combine relative coverage with allele balance at informative heterozygous sites, segment the genome and fit states; a matched normal helps; a total-copy profile alone cannot separate 1+1 from 2+0; homozygous sites are uninformative.
Copy state does not establish phase, gene inactivity, expression, dependency or drug response; bulk fits can hide subpopulations and unsampled lesions.
Fictional teaching exercise: Two A copies and no B copies under an adequate model is copy-neutral LOH: not deleted and not proven inactive.

For copy-state analysis, record tumour and suitable normal DNA, extraction consumption, relative depth and informative-site balance, segmentation, total/major/minor copies and purity/ploidy uncertainty. Reanalysis alone needs no tissue. Low purity, uninformative sites and ambiguous fits limit inference; amplification and functional-loss criteria are method-specific.

records.name: TPM, FPKM and raw counts (expression units)
records.tldr: RNA count units depend on what was counted, the normalisation denominator and any transcript-length adjustment.
records.summary: Raw RNA tables can contain assigned reads, fragments or model-estimated counts. Counts per million divide by a named library denominator. Transcripts per million first adjust for transcript length and scale the adjusted values to a total of one million; effective length depends on the quantifier. FPKM uses a different denominator and does not in general sum to a fixed total. UMI molecule counting and three-prime tag workflows need their own rules. Composition scaling, batch handling and statistical comparison remain separate questions; no single transformed unit is the universal model input.

links.label: Salmon: fast and bias-aware quantification of transcript expression (Nature Methods 2017)
Wikipedia

notes: Start from the counting unit (reads, fragments, estimated counts); a UMI is a tag added before amplification that reduces duplicate counting; it is a counting aid, not normalisation, and uncaptured molecules remain unobserved.
CPM divides a feature count by a stated library denominator and multiplies by one million; always state which denominator.
TPM first adjusts for transcript length then scales to one million across included transcripts; effective length suits some models and is not a drop-in rule for 3-prime tag or UMI workflows.

Between-sample methods address composition: abundant messages take library share; TMM and DESeq2 size factors estimate scaling under assumptions and do more than divide by totals; broad shifts challenge them.
Fictional teaching exercise: Two transcripts with 100 fragments each and lengths 1 and 2 kb: CPM 500,000 each; rates 100 and 50 sum 150; TPM about 666,667 and 333,333.
Normalisation does not repair batch effects or recover absolute molecules, cell origin, protein activity or benefit; a normalised difference still needs design and a model.

Rescaling an existing feature table needs its counting unit, annotation, library metadata, denominator and any length rule; adding molecular tags requires library preparation. Report CPM, TPM or the chosen model input explicitly. Runtime, controls, replicates and composition checks vary. Wrong units, tag errors, broad shifts and incompatible annotations undermine filters/comparisons; normalisation alone does not validate a clinical test.

records.name: Genome-wide loss of heterozygosity (gLOH)
records.tldr: This assay-defined score summarizes genomic regions that lost previously different allelic information. It can reflect a past repair defect, including changes that preserve total DNA copy count.
records.summary:
Loss of heterozygosity means loss of previously distinct allelic information at a locus. It can accompany copy loss or occur with a copy-neutral allelic change; tumor purity and ploidy complicate inference. Genome-wide loss of heterozygosity summarizes affected interrogated regions according to the assay’s definition. It is studied as a genomic scar associated with some homologous-recombination-repair defects, rather than a direct measurement of present repair function.

The threshold belongs to the assay and setting. ARIEL2 part 1 prespecified 14 percent or more as LOH high in its ovarian-cancer analysis; this does not establish a universal cutoff. Pan-cancer studies found elevated gLOH associated with biallelic BRCA1/2 alterations and with a core set of other repair-gene alterations, with effects differing by cancer context. Monoallelic calls and an HRR-gene-list label are not interchangeable with those findings. TP53 loss was independently associated with gLOH in the Westphalen analysis.

In 3,476 prostate tumors, Chung and colleagues found BRCA1/2, ATR and FANCA alterations associated with high gLOH, while CDK12-altered tumors, about 6 percent of that cohort, were infrequently gLOH high. The study did not correlate these findings with clinical outcomes. Such associations support gene-specific biological questions; they do not establish an individual patient’s drug benefit or current treatment eligibility.

notes: A scar is different from a present functional defect. gLOH does not by itself establish which repair gene is affected, whether both alleles are inactivated, or whether repair remains impaired. A tumour can retain an earlier genomic scar after its functional state changes.

There is no single gLOH-high cutoff across assays and cancers. ARIEL2 part 1 used a prespecified assay threshold in ovarian carcinoma. Preserve the assay, specimen and reporting context, including uncertainty near a categorical threshold.

Tumour sequencing and clinical hereditary testing answer different questions. The historical TRITON2 study reported similar objective response rates in germline- and somatic-BRCA groups in its enrolled prostate-cancer population; that result is not a current treatment-access rule or evidence that a negative hereditary assay excludes acquired tumour variants.

A local LOH state and a genome-wide LOH score have different scope. In an idealised informative A/B region, 1+1 and 2+0 both total two copies, but only 2+0 loses one sequence version. A total-copy profile alone cannot distinguish them. Allele-aware inputs and purity/ploidy assumptions constrain the call; a genome-wide score does not identify the retained sequence, phase a mutation or directly measure current gene function.

records.name: TMB-high (tumour mutational burden)
records.tldr: This result reports a high density of acquired DNA changes under a specified test’s rules.
records.summary: Tumour mutational burden estimates the density of eligible acquired DNA changes under assay-specific counting, filtering and calibration rules. Identical units do not make different assays interchangeable. FDA’s 16 October 2026 conversion of the U.S. tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab indication to traditional approval changed its criterion from 10 to at least 13 mutations per megabase. The indication covers adults and children with unresectable or metastatic solid tumours, measured by an FDA-authorised test, that progressed after prior treatment and have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. A research value or a high category alone does not establish these conditions or guarantee benefit.

FDA states that efficacy supporting traditional approval was not confirmed for TMB from 10 to below 13 mutations per megabase. This does not establish universal lack of benefit or a contraindication below 13; other indications and individual evidence have separate scope.

Published cohort frequencies and study thresholds below retain their original assay, cutoff and population. They must not be substituted for the current drug-label criterion. Blood and tissue estimates also require their own validation.

Triple-negative breast cancer: 10 or more mutations per megabase in about 5% of breast cancers, more often HR-negative/HER2-negative and metastatic (8.4% versus 2.9%; Barroso-Sousa 2020), 4.1% of 123 TCGA triple-negative exomes (cBioPortal) and 18% of 62 pretreated metastatic TNBC patients on immunotherapy trials, where it went with progression-free survival of 12.5 versus 3.7 months (Barroso-Sousa 2020, Clin Cancer Res). These study cutoffs do not establish the current U.S. tumour-agnostic indication, which requires at least 13 mutations per megabase by an FDA-authorised test, progression after prior treatment and no satisfactory alternatives in unresectable or metastatic solid tumours; APOBEC rather than mismatch repair drives most hypermutated TNBC.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: 10 or more mutations per megabase in 1 to 2% of panel-tested tumours (35 of 2,336 MSK-IMPACT samples, median 3.46; cBioPortal), and TMB-high at the stricter 20 threshold together with MSI-high in 0.5% of samples (Singhi 2019); 4.5% of KRAS wild-type against 1% of mutant tumours (Philip 2022). Exome medians are about 1 per megabase, so the panel figure is a convention rather than a biological rate.

Colorectal cancer: 10 or more mutations per megabase in 15 to 19% of panel-tested tumours (1,340 of 7,237 in crc_msk_2026, median 6.05; cBioPortal), but almost all of that group is the MSI-high group (median 56.9) plus the POLE-hotspot group (median 172.1), against 5.7 in microsatellite-stable disease. These assay-defined cohort frequencies do not by themselves establish eligibility or benefit. The October 2026 U.S. tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab indication requires at least 13 mutations per megabase by an FDA-authorised test, an unresectable or metastatic solid tumour that progressed after prior treatment, and no satisfactory alternatives; the separate MSI-H or dMMR colorectal indication has its own criteria.

Gallbladder cancer: median 4.1 non-synonymous mutations per megabase on the 505-gene MSK-IMPACT panel with 28 of 244 samples (11.5%) at 10 or more (cBioPortal gbc_mskcc_2022), against a median of 0.82 per megabase by whole-exome sequencing (Nepal 2021) and TMB-high in 1.3% (1 of 79) of Indian patients on mixed panels (Suryavanshi 2025). These study cutoffs do not establish eligibility for the current U.S. tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab indication: at least 13 mutations per megabase by an FDA-authorised test, unresectable or metastatic solid tumour, progression after prior treatment and no satisfactory alternative treatment options.

Lung cancer: this is where mutational burden was discovered as a predictor and where it failed as a selector. It is a real correlate: burden tracks response, progression-free survival and overall survival for single-agent PD-(L)1 blockade within every PD-L1 stratum in 1,552 patients, with response 57% where burden and PD-L1 are both high and 8.7% where neither is (Ricciuti 2022), and tissue burden of 175 or more mutations per exome selected benefit from pembrolizumab monotherapy in KEYNOTE-042 (overall survival hazard ratio 0.62 against 1.09 below the cut) (Mok 2023). But the threshold moves with the assay and the unit, the data-derived cut in the largest cohort was more than 19 mutations per megabase rather than the historical U.S. tumour-agnostic threshold of 10, and in the trials of pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, the regimen most patients receive, continuous burden predicted nothing in either histology (Garassino 2023). FDA’s October 2026 conversion added prospective Cohort M to the earlier retrospectively analysed cohorts. The current U.S. tumour-agnostic indication requires at least 13 mutations per megabase by an FDA-authorised test, an unresectable or metastatic solid tumour that progressed after prior treatment and no satisfactory alternatives; lung-cancer-specific indications have separate criteria.
